series_label: People using at least basic drinking water services (% of population)
source_or_custodian: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (washdata.org), via World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI) on Data360
release_or_vintage: JMP publication date 2025-08-25 (accessed 2025-09-30); Data360 version date 2026-07-01; WDI release calendar: every odd year in September
status_or_notes: Annual series; server covers 2000-2024 for Nigeria. No value for 2025 is available (the server's time range ends 2024). Values are JMP modelled estimates (linear regression on household surveys such as DHS and MICS, censuses and administrative data), not direct annual observations. Nigeria values are at ~1.62 percentage points per year from 2000 to 2023, with a smaller step from 2023 to 2024. Same concept is also in WB_CLEAR_JMP_DW_AB (2000-2022) and WB_HCP_UNICEF_WATER (2000-2024), which were not queried.
definition: The percentage of people using at least basic water services. This indicator encompasses both people using basic water services as well as those using safely managed water services. Basic drinking water services is defined as drinking water from an improved source, provided collection time is not more than 30 minutes for a round trip. Improved water sources include piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected dug wells, protected springs, and packaged or delivered water.
citation: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) for Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene (washdata.org); authors listed: Richard Paul Johnston (WHO), Tom Slaymaker (UNICEF). Accessed via World Bank Data360, World Development Indicators (WB_WDI).
